summary: Feed s053_single to APM is degraded: 50% of traffic is untagged and required VLAN 20 is completely missing, breaking segmentation visibility. All other checks (duplicates, encryption, one-way, oversize, drops, overload, truncation, tunnels) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or TAP aggregation port is stripping 802.1Q tags or is configured as access/untagged instead of 802.1Q trunk. Required VLAN 20 is not forwarded to the APM tool port, resulting in 50% untagged packets.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM requires VLANs 10 and 20 to segment and correlate application transactions by tenant/tier. With VLAN 20 missing and half the traffic untagged, the APM cannot attribute performance metrics to the correct VLAN, loses transaction context, and has blind spots for VLAN 20 applications.

recommended_fix.why: Restore 802.1Q trunk preservation on the broker ingress/egress to forward VLANs 10 and 20 intact to the APM. This restores the VLAN context the APM needs without altering payload or load.
